scope: Approved message-title revision. Existing numbering and exhibit content retained. No prior-engagement comparison or new forecast inferred.

titles.title: Diesel dominates net imports; additional Vopak volumes still need customer evidence
titles.basis: Overview findings: 2024 net trade and unquantified customer opportunity.

titles.title: Net diesel imports were more than three times net petrol imports in 2024
titles.basis: Existing SARS exhibit: diesel 9.997 versus petrol 3.081 bn litres.

titles.title: Gauteng, KZN and Western Cape accounted for 68.6% of reported fuel sales in 2022
titles.basis: Existing 2022 provincial petrol and diesel table; jet excluded in exhibit.

titles.title: Gauteng led provincial sales through 2022; later estimates do not establish a shift
titles.basis: Observed provincial history and explicitly held-share 2024 petrol estimates.

titles.title: Provincial sales locate demand, but do not show where imported fuel is delivered
titles.basis: Sales totals are sourced; origin split is authored illustration.

titles.title: The car fleet grew 3% in 2025 while road-freight payload was broadly flat
titles.basis: Native charts: car index 102.954 and road payload 99.528; 2024=100. No fuel-demand elasticity inferred.

titles.title: OCGT generation fell 79% from FY2024 to FY2026, reducing a driver of diesel use
titles.basis: Native Eskom+IPP generation index: 100 to 20.97997. This is generation, not a measured 79% fall in diesel litres.

titles.title: Published refinery capacity halved between 2020 and 2022; new capacity remains conditional
titles.basis: Existing capacity series: 718 to 358 thousand bbl/day; capacity distinguished from output.

titles.title: Demand growth alone cannot determine imports, accessible volumes or storage needs
titles.basis: Existing framework separates demand, domestic supply, customer access and operations.

titles.title: Rail diversion and lower OCGT use could offset freight-led diesel growth
titles.basis: Proposed lever relationships, not a calibrated forecast result.

titles.title: Flight activity and fuel burn set jet demand; SAF changes its fossil-fuel share
titles.basis: Proposed aircraft-movement, fuel-burn and volumetric SAF levers in existing table.

titles.title: Fleet growth raises petrol demand; electrification and efficiency could offset it
titles.basis: Existing proposed fleet, mileage, BEV and new-cohort efficiency relationships; no forecast magnitude inferred.

titles.title: Road costs alone cannot establish the competitiveness of Durban and Lesedi
titles.basis: Illustrative road surface excludes other delivered-cost and service factors.

titles.title: Matola and Walvis Bay offer alternative gateways; their impact on Durban is unproven
titles.basis: Published gateway storage and schematic routes; handled volumes and competitive access unresolved.

titles.title: Published Vopak tankage does not establish spare fuel capacity at Durban or Lesedi
titles.basis: Mixed-product gross capacity distinguished from compatible working space.

titles.title: Illustrative tank handling cannot establish a regional fuel surplus or shortage
titles.basis: Unverified turnover, incomplete inventory and overlapping coastal/inland flows.

titles.title: Additional Durban and Lesedi volumes depend on customer access, not national demand alone
titles.basis: Existing site implications table identifies customer destinations, routes and usable capacity evidence.

titles.title: Baseline reconciliation and assumption review are active; forecast runs follow reviewed inputs
titles.basis: Existing active-work table and stated delivery dependencies.

titles.title: Manish's handback needs source decisions and agreed inputs before integration
titles.basis: Existing proposed handback priorities and Nigel review decisions; no acceptance implied.

titles.title: Inter-terminal transfers can count the same fuel twice and overstate unique deliveries
titles.basis: Existing illustrative transfer example and stock-change qualification.

titles.title: Route limits, commercial access and existing business reduce the addressable opportunity
titles.basis: Illustrative screening waterfall; no actual opportunity quantified.

titles.title: Additional throughput requires new tanks only if existing usable capacity is insufficient
titles.basis: Illustrative stock calculation requires verified flows, inventory policy and operating constraints.

titles.title: At fixed tankage, three monthly turns imply three times the handling of one turn
titles.basis: Existing sensitivity is handling at fixed tankage, not storage sizing at fixed throughput.

titles.title: Sales and trade establish market scale; supply origins and fuel-use attribution remain open
titles.basis: Existing baseline trace table.

titles.title: The outlook still depends on unverified rail, fleet, refinery and route assumptions
titles.basis: Existing market-change trace table.

titles.title: Vopak market share and new investment needs remain unquantified
titles.basis: Existing two-row asset-outlook trace table.
